items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names reveal intent (`model_id`, `revision`, `q_emb`, `d_embs`, `ranked_indices`, `fifth_doc`) and short comments label each step. The script is short and reads in a straight line.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Debug output was left in: a `print("Rankings:")` loop dumps every document. The file sits in `scratch/run_retrieval.py`. It is one flat script, and the task name "T2Retrieval" was picked by trial and error.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There is no tie check on the similarities and nothing checks that at least 5 docs exist. The task name `"T2Retrieval"` is a magic string. On the plus side, files are opened with `with`, blank lines are filtered, and there is no swallowed-exception code.

items.name: Ranking details handled correctly
items.evidence: The model and revision are pinned via `mteb.get_model`, query and passage prompt types are used, and the dot product runs on normalized ST embeddings, so it equals cosine. It takes `ranked_indices[4]` and filters blank lines, but has no tie guard.
